title: A new HATETRIS record: 4,178 lines (Mon 16 Nov)
summary: @qntm.org, who keeps the record pages for the game HATETRIS on his own site, announced on Mon 16 Nov at 17:58Z: "We have a new HATETRIS record, 4,178 lines by skidikipopop!" (80 likes). In replies to his own post he added four things. The replay "takes several hours to run to completion in real time", and replays are now too large to express comfortably in the encoding used so far, so he will probably write them in raw format. The record came from a Tetris engine first meant for a bot competition, Botris, and modified to play against the HATETRIS AI. The player hopes to share source code. And the same player found "a new shortest loop for HATETRIS Mild, at 14 lines (4 lines to set the well up, 10 lines per loop iteration). The previous record was 7+10 = 17." The posts link to qntm.org/records ("HATETRIS high score progression") and qntm.org/loops ("Loops in HATETRIS"). No member of the cluster replied in the thread as the digest holds it.

posts.text:
You can find the replay here but be warned that it takes several hours to run to completion in real time

We're also now at the point where the replays are far too large to comfortably express using Base2048 - text editors and clipboard interfaces seem to struggle
I'm probably going to express replays in raw format in the future ("DURDRDRUUDUDLDDD...") because this is much easier to handle in practice even if it is quite a lot more verbose

skidikipopop's record comes from a Tetris engine originally intended to play in the PvP bot competition, Botris. This engine received some modifications to work against the HATETRIS AI. Here's some sample gameplay from that competition
links: https://youtube.com/watch?v=SLcKEeNpDTw (Cobra vs inf upstack (ALL SPINS) - Botris Battle Round 3)
